findings.title: A stalled command freezes ticket pickup
findings.description: `TimeoutStartSec=infinity` leaves the oneshot service running indefinitely if one of the runner's synchronous GitHub or git commands hangs. Because the timer schedules its next start only after the service becomes inactive, no later tick can recover the run or pick up another ticket.

findings.title: Fresh installs cannot start ticket pickup
findings.description: `ensureLabels()` runs only after the ready-ticket query returns a result, so it cannot create `ready-for-agent` when that label is absent. On a fresh repository, the owner cannot apply the missing label through the documented setup, and every timer tick finds no ready tickets and skips bootstrap again.

findings.title: Refused tickets can stall the backlog
findings.description: The refusal handler passes the new `agent-refused` labels to `setLabels()` without creating them, then catches an edit failure and exits successfully. If either label does not already exist, the ticket keeps `ready-for-agent`; because the queue checks it first on every tick, later tickets never start.

findings.title: Agents can publish host secrets in PRs
findings.description: `agent()` grants host-side `Read`, `Glob`, and `Grep` access while its new permission rules deny only a short list of home directories. An unattended agent that reads an unlisted secret such as `~/.npmrc` can put it in `.agent/pr-body.md`, which `checkAndPush()` publishes to the repository’s PR.

findings.title: Agent-run tests can expose host secrets
findings.description: `agent()` inherits the runner's entire environment and permits execution of agent-written JavaScript through test commands, while `npmTest()` executes that code again outside the Claude tool restrictions. An unattended run can therefore read host credentials, make network or GitHub API requests without a denied command, or alter files outside the worktree; the post-run footprint only compares selected GitHub resources.

findings.title: Uncommitted fixes can receive a green PR
findings.description: `agent()` logs dirty worktree files without rejecting them, and `checkAndPush()` tests that worktree before pushing only `HEAD`. If an implementation or test fix remains uncommitted, the runner can report passing tests and publish a commit that does not contain the code it tested.

findings.title: Concurrent runners can share a ticket
findings.description: The stale-lock path checks the timestamp, unlinks the lock and reacquires it in separate operations, without verifying that the file being removed is still the stale one. If two invocations attempt recovery together, one can remove the other's newly acquired lock, allowing both to operate on the same ticket and worktree.

findings.title: New unit tests cannot join the test run
findings.description: The unattended skill directs the agent to add `tests/*.test.mjs`, but forbids changes to `package.json`. Because `test:unit` explicitly names its existing test files, a new unit file is absent from `npm test`; its red commit fails the factory proof rather than becoming a runnable regression test.

findings.title: Runtime errors can pass the red-test proof
findings.description: `proveRed()` accepts any failing line containing an extracted new test name; it does not establish that an assertion failed. A newly named test that throws a `TypeError` or `ReferenceError` satisfies the check, so the PR can claim red-to-green proof without the assertion failure required by the work-ticket process.

findings.title: Active PRs can lose their latest review
findings.description: `issueComments()` fetches only the first 100 comments, but `qodoReview()` and `ownerAsks()` treat that response as the complete PR conversation. Once later Qodo summaries or `/agent` requests fall on another page, the loop misses them and can time out waiting for a review or ignore the owner's request.

findings.title: Old label history can authorize pickup
findings.description: `labelledByOwner()` selects the last matching label event from only the first 100 issue events, rather than the event that produced the current `ready-for-agent` label. On an issue whose later relabeling is on another page, the runner can accept an old owner-applied event as authorization or overlook a valid recent owner action.
